analysis.title: DeskTalk - FOMC holds as expected in 10-2 vote
key_insights: The FOMC left rates unchanged as expected in a 10-2 vote. Fed governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented in favor of a 25bp rate hike.
Cook's dissent was the biggest surprise. Many had expected Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan to favor a hike instead.
Citi economists read Logan's vote to hold as a willingness to wait until December before further tightening, a modestly dovish signal relative to expectations.
The policy statement was largely unchanged. The main edit upgraded the description of economic activity to "strong" from "solid".
The committee said the accumulation of more information will help it decide the policy stance.
The initial market reaction was mostly subdued: front-end yields unchanged, the dollar firmer, SPX +20bps and NDX +5bps. OIS odds for a December move rose to 87% from 83%.

macro_indicators.reading: Rates unchanged, 10-2 vote, two dissents in favor of a 25bp hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hold was expected, but two hawkish dissents show a tightening bias on the committee.

macro_indicators.indicator: OIS-implied odds of a December hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets price a December move as highly likely, and the odds edged higher after the decision.

risk_factors: Two hawkish dissents (Cook and Hammack) suggest risk of faster tightening than the committee's hold implies.
Chair Warsh's press conference at 2:30 could shift the market reaction.
vol_and_positioning: SPX is trying to snap a losing streak across the past 6 FOMC meetings, with SPX +20bps and NDX +5bps after the statement.
